tagline: OV-104 — fourth Shuttle. Flew final mission STS-135 (2011), final Hubble servicing STS-125 (2009), deployed Galileo + Magellan
dispatch: Atlantis, OV-104, flew the bookends of the Shuttle's greatest partnerships. It made the most dockings with the Russian station Mir, opening the era of US-Russian cooperation, and it flew STS-125, the final, daring servicing mission that left the Hubble Space Telescope good for another decade. In July 2011 Atlantis flew STS-135, the 135th and last Shuttle mission — the flight that closed thirty years of reusable American spaceflight and left the Space Station it had helped build in orbit above.
description: Fourth operational orbiter; first flight STS-51-J (1985-10-03) was a classified DoD mission. Highlights: deployed Magellan (STS-30, 1989) and Galileo (STS-34, 1989) — the two planetary probes that opened Venus and Jupiter to long-duration observation; flew 7 of the 9 Shuttle-Mir docking missions between 1995-1997; flew the final Hubble servicing mission STS-125 (2009-05) — the only post-Columbia non-ISS-rendezvous mission approved; flew STS-135 (2011-07) — the final Shuttle flight ever. On display at Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex since 2013.
best_known_for: Flew final Shuttle mission STS-135 (2011); deployed Galileo + Magellan; final Hubble servicing STS-125
